# Establishment log — popol-vuh-006 (images 0024–0027)

Read 2026-11-24 from source/pages/i0024 (after the first word `cut.`), i0025, i0026 and the first line of
i0027, in six-line strips at native size with 1.3–1.6× crops of every doubtful word, checked word by word
against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines 20098–20470). Start: `Cate cut ta xebec ꜩamal …` (0024 line 1, after `cut.`,
the end of popol-vuh-005). End: the last line of 0026 (`… quih acanoc ta chuꜩinoc, v-`) runs over to the first
line of 0027 (`cotobahic, xcha vloc Zipacna chiri pahul,`); the part ends there, with Zipacna's answer from
the pit. The next sentence, `Ma cu are cu cot …` (0027 line 2), belongs to popol-vuh-007.

Content: the old couple and the boys at Vucub Caquix's house; his teeth and eyes are "cured"; he dies, and
Chimalmat; the boys' arm is restored; the new episode (Ximénez's large V, `Vae chi cute vbanoh chic Zipacna`):
Zipacna carries the four hundred boys' roof-beam, and they plot to kill him in a pit.

## Folios
Counting as 004–005 did (0024 = 7v): 0025 = 8r, 0026 = 8v, 0027 = 9r → `fols. 7v–9r`. The crops of 0024
and 0026 carry 7 and 8 at the top left, consistent with the folio doubt in QUESTIONS.md (2026-11-24); the
earlier count is kept.

## Letter rule used (002–005's rules, unchanged)
- q-shaped letter (+ u) where Brasseur has g → ꜫ, u dropped: `hutaꜫih`, `choꜫitahic` (B. ch'ogitahic),
  `vꜫexel` ×3 (MS `vquexel`; B. u gexel), `vꜫinomal`.
- tresillo → ꜫ: `vꜫab` (0025), `qui ꜫab` (MS `quiꜫab`).
- g-shaped letter → ꜭ: `ꜭaholab` (all), `ꜭahol`, `ꜭaxtoꜭ` (both letters), `ahꜭun` (B. aheun; MS `ahgun`), gh → ꜭh:
  `xꜭha`, `xeꜭha`, `caꜭha`, `ca ꜭhauic` (B. chauic), `coh ꜭha`, `xuꜭhaxic`, `xuꜭhax`.
- q-shaped letter where Brasseur has q (= ꜭ): `ruꜭ` ×2, `cuꜭ` ×2, `Vꜭux Cah`, `chi iꜭux` (MS `chiiqux`),
  `cat ꜭohe`, `Ꜭo pa` (B. Qo-pa).
- q-shaped letter where Brasseur has k (plain q): `chaquimah` (B. chakimah) kept as qu.
- plain c kept where Brasseur has q, k or g: `vcalibal` (B. u galibal), `ca ca tocobah` (B. ka tokobah),
  `vcoxom`, `ca coxouic`, `hocom bac` ×2 (B. hogom bak), `cahoc`, `coto`/`xucoto`/`vcotic` (B. qot-),
  `xcam qui naoh` (B. x-qam), `xquicam` (B. qam), `xcah` (B. x-c'ah).
- plain ch where the verb of speaking is elsewhere gh: `“Vꜩ bala,” cha cut` (0026) and `xcha vloc Zipacna`
  (0027 line 1) — the image has c, not g, in both; printed as written (B. cha).
- tz ligature → ꜩ: `ꜩamal`, `eꜩeyah`, `ꜩucubei`, `iꜩucubal`, `Cuꜩin`, `quiꜩih`, `vꜩ` (all), `iꜩel`, `vꜩih`,
  `ꜩac`, `ꜩalanem`, `chuꜩinoc`.
- ß-ligature read ti (as 005): `atit` (all), `catinic` (MS `caßnic`), `xtiquitax` (MS `xßquitax`),
  `xutiquiba` (MS `xußquiba`), `vcotic` (MS `vco-|ßc`), `xuticoto` (MS `xußcoto`).

## Struck through by Ximénez (left out)
- 0024: `hocombac [x]ri xa zaqui ixim` — an x struck before `ri`; not printed.
- 0025: about ten lines, after `… xupunabeh varal chuvach vleu.` and before `naual atit`, are struck through
  line by line (they begin `huyab chic xquiꜭimic ta xꜭaha-|panoc …` and include `… omuch chi ꜭaholab xeꜭha cut …
  lacabebal`); Brasseur prints none of it. Apparently a passage copied out of place and cancelled. Not printed.
- 0026: `pachal [x]cahoc pa hul` — an x blotted out before `cahoc`; not printed.
- 0024: `naquion [ch] qui chi cunah` — `ch` struck at the line end; not printed.
- 0024: `xa cu nimac vachih chic [..] ca ꜭhauic` — a blotted letter group before `ca`; not printed.

## Supralinear
- 0024: `ca ca tocobah` — the second `ca` is written above the line; printed in place.

## Doubtful readings
- `xe icouic`, `xe icou` (0024, 0025): MS `taxe icouic`, `taxei-|cou`; B. `x-e iqouic`. Brasseur's q would be ꜭ;
  the image has plain c in all three. Printed c.
- `ri yaaxel hupir chacap` (0024): clear in the image as `ri yaaxel`; the OCR of Brasseur is garbled here.
  Meaning of `yaaxel` unknown (B. French: 'we share and give them half'). Printed as written.
- `Ma ivalcual ri ivachbilan` (0024): MS `maiv alcual ri ivachbilan`; divided Ma + ivalcual, the second-person
  plural possessive joined as in `ivachbilan` and `iꜩucubal`.
- `ca cuxuuic` (0024): MS `cacuxuuic`; B. `ca coxuvic`; earlier on the page `ca coxouic`. Printed as written.
- `chuiub vehe chic ri ve` (0024): MS `chuiub vehe`; B. `ch'u yub v'ehe`. Meaning inferred ('they are all
  loose').
- `chi too vloc` (0024): MS `chi|too vloc`; B. `ch'y too uloc`. Printed as written.
- `zac huluhuh` (0025): MS `zac` at the line end, `huluhuh` on the next line, no hyphen; B. one word
  `zakhuluhuh`. Divided; the z has a long tail that looks like a cedilla.
- `Huzucu` (0025): MS `Huzu-|cu`; 005 printed `huzuc`. Printed as written here.
- `ahꜭun` (0025): MS `ahgun`; B. `aheun` (OCR). The healer word; ꜭ by the letter rule, though the modern word
  is ajkun with plain k. The drafter should note it.
- `xtiquitax vcoc` (0025): MS `xßquitax v-|coc`; B. `x-tiqui ta x-uq-oc`. Meaning inferred ('it was set, it
  went in').
- `Vucub` (all): the second letter often looks like v (`vvcub`); printed Vucub as in 005 and the house table.
- `e hur vi` (0025): MS `ehurui`; divided as Brasseur (`e hur vi`).
- `apa copon vi` (0026): MS `apacopon`; B. `Apa c'opon vi`. Printed as written.
- `xuteleba ca acanoc` (0026): MS `xuteleba ca|acan oc`; B. `x-u teleba cu akan-oc`. The image has ca; acanoc
  joined as on 0026's last line (`acanoc`).
- `chi ca ban chire` (0026): MS `chicaban` or `chicahan` (b and h alike here); B. `chi ka ban`. Printed b.
- `hun vi chi hul` (0026): MS `hun|vichihul`; divided as Brasseur.
- `xuticoto` (0026): MS `xußcoto`; B. `x-u qoto`. Perhaps `xutic coto` ('he began to dig'); printed as written.
- `xcolotah vi` (0026): MS `xcolotah vi`; B. `x-colo-tah vi`.
- `Qui na nu coto; ve xquix nu ziquih acanoc` (0026): MS `quinanucoto ve xquix nuzi-|quih`; punctuated as Brasseur.

## Word division and paragraphs (ours)
As in 002–005. Paragraphs follow Ximénez's stops and Brasseur's paragraphing; each exchange of speeches is kept
in one paragraph so the quotation marks close within it. The four hundred boys' plan contains the words they
will say to Zipacna (`Ha cama caha vleu pa hul`); not set in inner quotation marks (the checks forbid ’), so the
drafter must show the embedded speech in the English. The large V of `Vae chi cute vbanoh chic Zipacna` (0025)
begins the Zipacna episode as its own paragraph.
